clue.text: Fruit tree brings back the Fall? That's right!

indicators.note: brings back tells us the word for the Fall is to be read from end to start

parts.note: the Fall of man is the lapse from grace
that is, in Latin id est, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: An exclamation about autumn and a fruit tree, as if the tree heralded the season's arrival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings back' turns LAPSE into ESPAL. 'The Fall' with a capital invites autumn, but it is the biblical lapse.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a fruit tree trained flat against a wall or trellis.

clue.text: Slip bolt

explanation.definitionFit: To slip away and to bolt both mean to get free and run off.

clue.text: Member of TV team, one succeeding Miss Gwynne in an earlier period

indicators.note: in places the actress and the one inside the word for an earlier period

parts.note: an earlier period is the past

indicators.note: succeeding means coming after, so the one follows the actress

parts.note: Nell Gwynne, the actress and mistress of Charles II
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone on a television panel follows in the footsteps of the Restoration actress Nell Gwynne.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwynne (or Gwyn) was a famous seventeenth-century English actress, mistress of King Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel show's team members sit on a panel, each one a guest on the show's bench.

clue.text: Doddery elder sheltering with a place out of the wind

indicators.note: sheltering means keeping safe inside, so the shuffled word holds the other pieces
doddery means shaky and unsteady, telling us the letters of elder totter into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shaky old man shelters in a spot away from the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doddery' signals the anagram of the old man, and 'sheltering' wraps those shuffled letters round the other two pieces. 'place out of the wind' is the sheltered side, used as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeward side is the side sheltered from the wind, the downwind side.

clue.text: Firmly put down journalist without honour

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the journalist goes round the honour

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist
the MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A reporter with no decorations is firmly dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking. The MBE is a British royal honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something firmly in a surrounding mass is to set it deep, as a post set in concrete.

clue.text: Sound measure

explanation.definitionFit: To sound the sea is to plumb its depth; as a noun it is a nautical unit of six feet.

clue.text: Design new part for port

indicators.note: to design is to plan or arrange, telling us the letters of new and part are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Advice to draw up a fresh component as a replacement for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major Belgian seaport on the Scheldt.

clue.text: Man will get round to give greeting

parts.note: a man will, contracted, is he'll
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A man will make the effort to say hi to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A word of salutation said on meeting someone or answering the phone.

clue.text: Rubber body needed on eastern exercise

parts.note: a body is a mass, as in a body of water
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A rubber body is required for some eastern exercise, as if describing gym equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' looks like the material; it is a person who rubs, a woman giving massages.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who gives massages, kneading and rubbing muscles for a living.

clue.text: Right winger is a dedicated athlete

parts.note: dedicated means loyal, faithful, true
a Blue is an athlete who has represented Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A loyal conservative is described as a committed sportsperson.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is a sportsperson chosen for Oxford or Cambridge against the other. Blue is also the colour of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch Tory loyalist; blue is the colour of the British Conservatives.

clue.text: They tell stories, and hurry to suppress the least revision

parts.note: to canter is to go at a brisk pace, to hurry
to bury a story is to suppress it

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, telling us the letters of least are rearranged

explanation.surface: Storytellers rush to hide the slightest edit to their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' rearranges LEAST to TALES. Chaucer's Canterbury Tales is a set of stories told by pilgrims.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaucer's pilgrims tell each other stories on the road, so the work is a collection of narratives.

clue.text: Head has a way to cut down the number of branches

definitions.text: to cut down the number of branches

parts.note: the poll is the head, as in a poll tax
taken as written
RD, short for road, is a way

explanation.surface: The head of a team finds a method to reduce the number of company branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'branches' reads like a firm's offices, but they are a tree's.
explanation.definitionFit: To lop a tree back to its trunk so that it sprouts a dense head of new shoots.

clue.text: Clumsy Eeyore's bad sight

indicators.note: clumsy means awkwardly put together, telling us these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name Eeyore with its possessive s, used for its letters

explanation.surface: Winnie-the-Pooh's donkey Eeyore has poor eyesight because he is clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of the possessive is needed in the fodder. Eeyore is the gloomy donkey in Winnie-the-Pooh.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly thing that offends the eye, a blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Air force's unexpected good fortune

explanation.definitionFit: A gust's force brings down fruit, and fruit blown from the tree came to mean any unlooked-for gain.

clue.text: A recent vehicle secured, on special order

indicators.note: secured means held fast, so the word for recent holds the vehicle

parts.note: late means recent, as in the late news
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A new car was obtained by placing a special order.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes ordered individually from the menu rather than as a set meal.

clue.text: Old prince, and where he got plastered?

explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan prince who took Helen; and plaster of Paris named after the French capital.

clue.text: File to cover up orally with a sign of disapproval

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file

indicators.note: orally means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the word for cover up

parts.note: to bury something is to cover it up

explanation.surface: Someone hides a nail file, and gets a rude noise of disapproval for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A raspberry is the rude noise made by blowing through the lips.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude spluttering noise blown through the lips to show contempt.

clue.text: Muscovite taken in by expert showing friendliness

indicators.note: taken in by means held within, so the word for expert surrounds the mineral

parts.note: able means skilled, expert
muscovite is a common form of the mineral mica

explanation.surface: A Russian from Moscow is fooled by a specialist who acts friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscovite' suggests a person from Moscow; it is a mineral, a form of mica.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and good-natured, as in an agreeable settlement between parties.

clue.text: Copper, say, buried under road

explanation.definitionFit: Copper is one of the elements of its kind; road metal is the broken stone laid as a road's base.

clue.text: Star striker

explanation.definitionFit: The morning star Venus; and an old name for a friction match that is struck.

clue.text: Pub patronised by fishwives?

parts.note: alewives are a kind of herring, so a drinking place for them is the pub built on their name

explanation.definitionFit: A tavern or inn where beer is served; the alewife is a North American fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Act better in old-fashioned drama

parts.note: out means unfashionable, as in out of date
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: Someone gives a better performance in a dated piece of theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' looks like stage acting; it means to perform in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: To outplay an opponent is to perform better than them.

clue.text: Changed colour: it faded again, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means heard aloud, so the spoken word for faded again is wanted

parts.note: to die away is to fade, so faded again is re-died

explanation.surface: Something that faded a second time is said to have switched colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed afresh, given a new colour by dyeing once more.

clue.text: Dog with a short coat needs drink

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
taken as written

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word coat loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A mutt with a clipped coat needs water.
explanation.walkthrough: Curacoa is a variant spelling of curacao, the orange liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange-flavoured liqueur from the Caribbean island of the same name.

clue.text: Mysterious letters, some for UNESCO

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Puzzling writing found among papers sent to the UN cultural agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Germanic alphabet characters, often used for magic or secret inscriptions.

clue.text: Gunners' set of figures may be estimated

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are the gunners of the British Army
a table is a set of figures

explanation.surface: An artillery unit's statistics may only be approximate.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable of being assessed or valued, as property is for local rates.

clue.text: Loot left in epidemic

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the word for epidemic

parts.note: rife means widespread, epidemic

explanation.surface: Plunder was abandoned during an outbreak of disease.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to ransack and steal from.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical sanction has regional effect by suppressing a broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the words regional effect by supply the letter pool
the letter a is suppressed, taken out of the pool

explanation.surface: A church ruling has a local impact, achieved by gagging a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suppressing a' removes an A from the letters of REGIONAL EFFECT BY before 'broadcast' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy once claimed exemption from secular courts, a privilege granted to the church's members.

clue.text: Guarantee to succeed without resistance

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for succeed goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: to ensue is to follow, to succeed
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A promise to win without opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain of something, to secure it.

clue.text: On reflection, married youth leader seen as naive (4-4) 22,881

indicators.note: on reflection means turned back as in a mirror, so the word for married is read backwards

parts.note: wed means married

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

parts.note: eyed means looked at, seen

explanation.surface: Looking back, the married young leader appears innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns WED into DEW. The trailing 22,881 and repeated count are the puzzle number caught by the OCR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentimental and innocent, moist-eyed with wonder.
